intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Israel election leaves both blocs short
items.text: Exit polls from Israel's general election suggest that neither Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot has won a majority. Two broadcasters projected 51 seats for each side in the 120-seat Knesset. Two Arab parties are expected to win 18 or 19 seats, so they could decide who forms the next government. Turnout was 77.7%, the highest at that stage since 1999. About 600,000 absentee ballots will be counted on Thursday.

gloss.exit poll: a survey of voters taken as they leave the place where they voted
gloss.bloc: a group of parties or countries that act together
gloss.majority: more than half of the votes or seats
gloss.turnout: the number of people who vote, as a share of those who can
gloss.absentee ballot: a vote sent in by someone who cannot go to the polling place

items.title: EU tells states to plan for 3C warming
items.text: The European Commission has proposed that member states should prepare for a world that is 3C warmer by 2100. Each country would have to name the authorities responsible for climate risks. Europe is warming at about twice the global average, and extreme weather caused more than €100 billion in damage this summer. Adapting to the changes will cost about €70 billion a year until 2050, but the plan includes no new funding. Only about a quarter of exposed assets are insured.

gloss.member state: a country that belongs to the European Union
gloss.extreme weather: very strong storms, floods, heatwaves or droughts
gloss.adapt: to change so that you can deal with a new situation
gloss.funding: money given for a particular purpose
gloss.insured: covered by a contract that pays money if something is damaged

items.title: Two men charged over RAF Fairford incident
items.text: Two men have been charged under the National Security Act after an incident at RAF Fairford in September. The base is used by US bombers. Prosecutors say five men drove vans loaded with petrol to the site on the orders of a handler who is believed to work for Iranian intelligence. Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, was released on bail, while Nouman Essghir, 24, was remanded in custody. Both will appear at the Old Bailey on 20 November. Iran denies coordinating the activity.

gloss.charge: to accuse someone officially of a crime
gloss.prosecutor: a lawyer who presents the case against someone in court
gloss.handler: a person who gives orders to a secret agent
gloss.bail: permission to stay free until a trial, often with conditions
gloss.remand: to keep someone in prison until their trial
gloss.intelligence: secret information about other countries, or the service that collects it

items.title: Fleetwood knock Arsenal out of the Cup
items.text: League Two side Fleetwood Town have knocked Arsenal out of the Carabao Cup. The match finished 1-1, and Fleetwood won 5-3 on penalties. Max Dowman was sent off for Arsenal, and manager Mikel Arteta's reaction to the red card has drawn criticism. Elsewhere, Bradford City reached the quarter-finals after they beat Peterborough United 2-0. Macaulay Gillesphey scored the first goal.

gloss.knock out: to defeat a team so that it leaves a competition
gloss.penalties: a way to decide a drawn match, with each team taking shots from close to the goal
gloss.sent off: ordered to leave the pitch by the referee for a serious foul
gloss.draw criticism: to make people say that you did something wrong
gloss.quarter-final: a match with eight teams left, played before the semi-finals

items.title: Shelton and Fils win in Basel
items.text: Top seed Ben Shelton of the United States won a tough match at the Swiss Indoors in Basel on Tuesday. He beat Aleksandar Kovacevic 6-7, 7-6, 7-6. France's Arthur Fils, the second seed, also went through after a 7-6, 7-5 win over Giovanni Mpetshi Perricard. Stan Wawrinka, who had a wild card, lost to Jiri Lehecka in straight sets. The tournament runs until 1 November.

gloss.seed: a top player placed in a good position in the draw
gloss.tie-break: a short game used to decide a set when the score is level
gloss.go through: to win and move on to the next round
gloss.wild card: a place in a tournament given to a player who did not qualify
gloss.straight sets: a win without losing a single set

items.title: Norwegian media sue Meta over AI plans
items.text: Ten Norwegian media groups, including the broadcaster NRK and Schibsted, have sued Meta in Oslo. Meta announced new terms for business accounts on Facebook and Instagram on 8 October. Publishers say the terms would let the company collect articles, photos and videos, even paywalled ones, to build AI products. They say the only way to opt out is to delete their accounts. Meta has postponed the launch to 20 November, and the publishers want a court to block the terms until the case is decided.

gloss.sue: to take someone to court to claim money or to stop them doing something
gloss.paywalled: available only to people who pay a subscription
gloss.opt out: to choose not to take part in something
gloss.postpone: to move to a later date
gloss.injunction: a court order that stops someone doing something

items.title: Scientists test 'mosquito toilets'
items.text: A scientist at Rutgers University in the US has built a device that he calls a mosquito toilet. It is a 3D-printed funnel with a water-repellent coating, and the liquid that mosquitoes leave behind slides into a tube. Researchers then check it for the genetic traces of viruses. In a test, waste from 50 mosquitoes found a complete West Nile virus genome and several viruses that may be new to science. The scientist says there is no reason for alarm.

gloss.funnel: a tube that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom
gloss.water-repellent: made so that water cannot soak into it
gloss.genome: all the genetic information of a living thing
gloss.early warning: a sign that tells you about a danger before it becomes serious

items.title: Neil Young sues Trump committee again
items.text: Neil Young has filed a new lawsuit over his 1989 song 'Rockin' in the Free World'. He says Trump's political committee plays the song at rallies without permission. Young sued Donald Trump's campaign over the same song in 2020, and that case ended with a settlement. He now says the committee has broken that agreement and has damaged his reputation. He is asking for $10 million and an order to stop the song being played in public.

gloss.lawsuit: a case in which one person or company takes another to court
gloss.copyright: the legal right to control who can use a song, book or film
gloss.settlement: an agreement that ends a legal dispute
gloss.break an agreement: to fail to do what you promised to do
gloss.damages: money that a court orders someone to pay for harm they caused

items.title: Pentagon puts Iran war cost at $47bn
items.text: The Pentagon has estimated that the war with Iran has cost $47.1 billion up to 16 October. Munitions make up more than 60% of the total, or about $29 billion, and a further $6.1 billion went on replacing damaged equipment. The figure is more than 25% higher than the estimate Pete Hegseth gave in July. It does not include $1.5 billion in other requested costs. The disclosure comes before the US elections on 3 November.

gloss.estimate: a rough calculation of the size or cost of something
gloss.munitions: weapons and ammunition used in war
gloss.disclosure: the act of making secret or new information public
gloss.make up: to form a certain part of a total

items.title: GTA VI is a reported 210 GB download
items.text: A report says that Grand Theft Auto VI will need a 210 GB download on consoles. The PlayStation Game Size account on X posted the figure first, and Insider Gaming says it has confirmed it. Players will be able to preload the game on 12 November, a week before the launch on 19 November. The standard edition costs $79.99. Rockstar Games has kept interest high in the game with trailers ahead of the launch.

gloss.preload: to download a game before its official release so you can play it at once
gloss.launch: the day when a new product first goes on sale
gloss.edition: a particular version of a game or book
gloss.corroborate: to give more evidence that something is true
gloss.keep up: to continue doing something at the same level
